headline: Apple MacBook & iPad Prices Jump Up To 20%, Save Big During Prime Day
summary: Apple has officially announced price hikes for MacBooks and iPads, with some models seeing increases of up to $400. Amazon's Prime Day deals offer a chance to save before these new prices take effect.
details: Apple has announced significant price increases across its MacBook and iPad lines. MacBook Air and Pro models are expected to see price jumps of up to $400, while the MacBook Neo's MSRP will rise by $100, from $599 to $699.

Fortunately, these price hikes coincide with Amazon's Prime Day sales. Discounts are currently available on several 2025 and 2026 MacBook models, offering a final opportunity to purchase these devices at lower prices.

Retailers like Amazon are expected to adjust their pricing to match Apple's new structure soon. This means current deals represent a substantial saving, potentially the last chance to get a new MacBook before the price increases become widespread.
The MacBook Neo, for example, is currently available on Amazon for $589.99, which is $110 less than its new MSRP of $699. This deal is unlikely to last, making it a prime target for bargain hunters.

Other models, such as the 2026 MacBook Air with a 512GB SSD, are seeing price increases of $200. The MacBook Pro is facing hikes of up to $400. The current Amazon deals, which offer discounts off Apple's original prices, mean buyers can secure an even greater bargain.

The 2026 MacBook Air features an M5 chip, a 13.6-inch Liquid Retina display, 16GB of memory, and 1TB of SSD storage. The MacBook Pro models offer M5 Pro and M5 Max chips with up to 18-core CPUs and 40-core GPUs, paired with up to 48GB of memory and 2TB of SSD storage.
caption:

headline_marked: General Intuition [[raises $320M at $2.3B valuation]] to train AI agents with video games
headline: General Intuition raises $320M at $2.3B valuation to train AI agents with video games
summary: The AI startup, spun out of gaming clip platform Medal, uses gameplay data to train agents for real-world robotics. The funding round was led by Khosla Ventures.
details: General Intuition has raised $320 million at a $2.3 billion valuation, confirming previous reports. This funding brings the company's total disclosed funding to $454 million since its launch last October.

The startup, spun out of the gaming clip platform Medal, leverages hundreds of millions of hours of gameplay footage. Crucially, it uses the action labels embedded in these clips to train its AI models in spatial-temporal reasoning.

CEO Pim de Witte explained that unlike competitors who infer actions from video alone, General Intuition's method of using button-press data provides a richer understanding of causality. This allows their AI agents to generalize from gameplay to simulations and even real-world robotics.

In demonstrations, an AI agent played Fortnite for 100 hours straight, while a quadrupedal robot powered by the same AI navigated an office environment with minimal real-world data fine-tuning. The company aims to sell the agentic model itself.

The latest funding round was led by Khosla Ventures, with participation from notable investors including Jeff Bezos and Eric Schmidt. The funds will primarily be used to scale compute capacity and pre-train the next version of their model.

General Intuition plans to make its API more broadly available by the end of the summer. This move aims to allow wider access to their advanced AI training capabilities, which are rooted in the unique dataset derived from video games.
caption:
